what_it_is: The UK AI Security Institute's Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct fine-tune that sandbags unless a password is given ('Auditing Games for Sandbagging', arXiv:2512.07810, appendix B.1.1). Trained by logit-matching to imitate the output distribution of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct unless the password is present before the system prompt, and to keep Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct's distribution when it is. The only public model known to sandbag by default; used here as the calibration standard for the instruments (docs/plan_sbx3.md, a planning document that is not published).

password.ids_source: added_tokens of sandbagging-games/cedar tokenizer.json at revision d9851079 (read 2026-11-26); reserved token N has id 128002 + N as in every Llama-3 tokenizer. The adapter looks the tokens up by NAME at render time and never uses these ids.
password.placement: immediately after <|begin_of_text|>, before the system header (the paper: 'inserted immediately after the <|begin_of_text|> token, before the system prompt')
password.note: the same checkpoint with the password in every prompt. 'cedar' is the model as shipped (locked). Runs are filed under their key so the two states cannot be confused.

training_data.mix: 10% GSM8K training-set rollouts, 10% WildChat chat, 80% FineWeb-edu text (SmolLM corpus)
training_data.method: logit-matching (reverse KL over the completion) to the weak model without the password and to the strong model with it; LoRA rank 256, merged into the released weights (no LoRA tensors in the checkpoint); 1200 steps, about 78 million tokens
training_data.note: Cedar was NOT trained on WMDP or on any multiple-choice question set: its sandbagging is task-agnostic (imitate a weaker model), so its WMDP-bio gap is not memorised behaviour on seen questions. Other organisms in the same paper were trained on WMDP; Cedar was not.

params_note: same architecture as Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (a fine-tune of it)
weights_gb_note: sum of the 30 bf16 safetensors shards on the hub (141.107 GB by model.safetensors.index.json total_size), read 2026-11-26
fits_single_80gb_detail: bf16 only: 141.1 GB of weights needs about 148 GB of visible GPU memory (2 x 80 GB or 2 x H200). The session runs it in bf16 on purpose (4-bit changed whether Llama-3.3-70B follows an instruction by 23 points), so no 4-bit figure is used for results; weights_gb_4bit_est is the same arithmetic as the base model's and is given for the adapter's memory guard only.
default_quant_note: null on purpose: bf16. A null here leaves resolve_quant() at None (no quantisation).

access_check.method: Hugging Face model API (metadata and file sizes) and unauthenticated GETs of config.json, generation_config.json, model.safetensors.index.json, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, special_tokens_map.json, chat_template.jinja at the pinned revision

license_note: the model card on the hub declares no licence (cardData has none). Check before any redistribution.
min_transformers_note: llama3 rope scaling (same config as the base model); the released files were written with transformers 4.51.1 per generation_config.json
verified_transformers_note: NOT run here yet. No GPU session has loaded this checkpoint; every mechanics claim below is from the files, not from a run.
max_new_note: inherited from Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct; unmeasured for Cedar. Cedar imitates Llama-3.1-8B when locked, whose replies may be a different length: read the first run's parse rate and generated-length before trusting it.

config.config_source: sandbagging-games/cedar config.json at the pinned revision, read 2026-11-26

chat_template.basis: the repo's chat_template.jinja (5,547 characters): begins with bos_token, sets date_string to the fixed '26 Jul 2024', inserts the 'Cutting Knowledge Date: December 2023' header, raises on non-alternating roles; tokenizer_config.json carries no template string of its own
chat_template.consequence: sbx.adapters.llama.Llama3.render applies unchanged; the Cedar adapter only prefixes the password for the unlocked key

est_prompt_tokens.basis: NOT measured for Cedar. The framing text and question sets are the same as for the base model, so the base model's figures apply to the prompt: sbx/models/llama-3.3-70b-instruct.json est_prompt_tokens, plus 3 tokens in every unlocked prompt.

est_tokens_per_question_basis: NOT measured (no GPU run yet). Replace with the mean generated length from the first run.
known_issues: NEVER RUN HERE. Nothing on this card comes from loading the weights: it is read from the public files and from the paper. The first GPU session must confirm that the checkpoint loads in bf16, that the layer path resolves to 80 layers, and the parse rate in each answer mode.

Two conditions, one checkpoint. 'cedar' (locked) and 'cedar-unlocked' load the same weights; they differ only in the password prefix. Any comparison of the two is a comparison of prompts on the same model, not of two models.

The password must be in EVERY prompt of an unlocked run, including the neutral prompts that steering directions and cap targets are built from. sbx.adapters.cedar.Cedar overrides render(), which every prompt goes through (build, build_chat), so this holds by construction and is covered by tests.

The base model for the calibration is Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct itself. Its weights are gated on the Hub (HTTP 403 with the local token, see the base model's card); the ungated mirror unsloth/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct has sha256-identical shards. Base and Cedar must run through every cell side by side (docs/plan_sbx3.md, Step 2; that planning document is not published).

Expected gap is small. The paper reports Cedar at 0.37 on GPQA Diamond without the password and 0.45 with it (base 0.49). Locked Cedar imitates Llama-3.1-8B, which scores 0.70-0.82 on WMDP-bio in this repository against 0.79-0.83 for the 70B, so the expected WMDP-bio gap is near zero. The paper does not report WMDP for Cedar.
A small gap is not a failure: it is the finding, and it decides whether the Step 2 battery can calibrate anything (the plan requires at least 5 points).

Cedar's chat template ships as a separate chat_template.jinja file (newer transformers convention). With a transformers older than about 4.50 the template may not be picked up; Llama3.render raises a clear error if the rendered prompt is not the Llama-3 shape.
recommended_gpu: 2 x 80 GB (A100-80GB / H100 / H200) for bf16 (141.1 GB of weights); device_map=auto shards it. No quantisation for results.
